# Spam Detection Examples

Real-world examples from microsoft/vscode issues labeled `spam`, with explanations. Profanity and personal data in the examples are paraphrased.

---

## SPAM Examples

### Example 1: Unfilled Template Placeholder

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294608

- **Title:** "Context error"
- **Body:** `ADD ISSUE DESCRIPTION HERE` followed by auto-generated web issue reporter template (Version, Commit, User Agent, Extension version)

**Why SPAM:**
1. The user never replaced the placeholder text "ADD ISSUE DESCRIPTION HERE" — they submitted the template as-is
2. "Context error" in the title is vague and describes no specific software behavior
3. All body content is auto-generated by the web issue reporter — the user wrote nothing

**Key lesson:** A template with its placeholder text still intact means the user didn't actually write anything. The title alone isn't enough if it doesn't describe a concrete problem.

---

### Example 2: Greeting as Title, No Body

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294444

- **Title:** "Hi"
- **Body:** *(empty)*

**Why SPAM:**
1. "Hi" is a greeting, not a bug report or feature request
2. Body is completely empty — zero technical content
3. No attempt whatsoever to describe a software problem

---

### Example 3: Profanity + Abusive Language + Auto-Filled Template (Code of Conduct Violation)

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294407

- **Title:** An inflammatory accusation that AI agents harm users
- **Body:** Contains profanity, violent and sexualized accusatory language, and slurs. Followed by auto-generated VS Code bug report template (system info, GPU status, A/B experiments).

**Why SPAM:**
1. The user's own text contains profanity and abusive language throughout
2. No concrete technical claim — no steps to reproduce, no expected vs actual behavior
3. The extensive system info (CPUs, GPUs, memory) is all auto-generated by VS Code's issue reporter
4. Violates code of conduct with inflammatory accusations and vulgar language

**Key lesson:** Even if an issue mentions a product feature by name, profanity and abusive language make it spam. The auto-filled template padding doesn't legitimize abusive content.

---

### Example 4: Keyboard-Mash Title + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294242

- **Title:** "Tttttt"
- **Body:** Empty bug report template — all fields blank (VS Code Version, OS Version, Steps to Reproduce all unfilled)

**Why SPAM:**
1. Title is repeated characters with no meaning — clearly accidental or test input
2. Body is the raw bug report template with every field left empty
3. No user-written content exists anywhere in the issue

---

### Example 5: Pure Profanity, No Content

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#293779

- **Title:** A single profane word
- **Body:** *(empty)*

**Why SPAM:**
1. Title is a single profane word with no technical meaning
2. Body is completely empty
3. Zero attempt to describe any software issue — this is just abuse

---

### Example 6: Email Address as Title + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#293789

- **Title:** A personal email address
- **Body:** Empty feature request template with placeholder comments only

**Why SPAM:**
1. Title is an email address — not a bug report or feature description
2. Body contains only the raw template placeholder text, unfilled
3. Likely submitted accidentally or by someone unfamiliar with issue trackers
4. Also exposes personal information (email) inappropriately

---

### Example 7: GitHub URL as Title + Link-Only Body

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294322

- **Title:** "https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/294317"
- **Body:** A quoted link to another issue, auto-generated from a comment cross-post

**Why SPAM:**
1. Title is just a URL — not a description of any problem
2. Body contains only a cross-posted link with no original content
3. The user added zero information — this is a duplicate shell with no substance

---

### Example 8: Profanity Throughout Despite Real Technical Content

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294147

- **Title:** "Can't turn your [profanity] copilot off and it keeps hanging all save actions and hindering development"
- **Body:** Contains extensive profanity and an obscene insult aimed at the company while describing a real settings issue with Copilot and save actions. Includes screenshots.

**Why SPAM:**
1. Pervasive profanity and slurs throughout, including an obscene insult targeting the company
2. Although there IS a real technical complaint buried in the text, the abusive language violates code of conduct
3. Slurs and insults are flagged **even if there is technical content alongside them**

**Key lesson:** An issue can describe a real problem AND still be spam when it is abusive: pervasive profanity, slurs, or insults aimed at people or the company. A few frustrated curse words in an otherwise genuine report are not enough. The user could refile without the abusive language.

---

### Example 9: Non-Technical Phrase (Non-English) + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#293748

- **Title:** "零接触" (Chinese for "zero contact")
- **Body:** Empty feature request template with placeholder comments only

**Why SPAM:**
1. "零接触" means "zero contact" — a non-technical phrase that doesn't describe any software behavior
2. Body is the raw feature request template, completely unfilled
3. Being in a non-English language doesn't make it spam — the lack of any technical content does
4. Compare with Example 17 below: non-English issues WITH technical content are CLEAN

---

### Example 10: Unrelated Content (Not About VS Code)

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#293672

- **Title:** "PANXIS(FULL LENGTH FEATURE)"
- **Body:** The title text repeated inside an HTML comment in a feature request template

**Why SPAM:**
1. "PANXIS" and "FULL LENGTH FEATURE" have nothing to do with VS Code or software development
2. The body rephrases the title inside an HTML comment — no technical content
3. The same user filed a follow-up (#293673) attaching a PDF screenshot of a video app — completely unrelated to VS Code

**Key lesson:** Issues about topics entirely unrelated to the project are spam, even if the author uses the template structure.

---

### Example 11: Issue Number as Title + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#294034

- **Title:** "#292434"
- **Body:** Empty bug report template — all fields blank

**Why SPAM:**
1. Title is just an issue number reference with no description
2. Body is a completely unfilled bug report template
3. If the intent was to reference another issue, a comment on that issue would be appropriate — not a new empty issue

---

### Example 12: Vague Technical Title + Unfilled Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#305599

- **Title:** "Invalid string length issue"
- **Body:** Bug report template with only HTML comments and empty fields (VS Code Version, OS Version, Steps to Reproduce all blank). No user-written content.

**Why SPAM:**
1. Title sounds technical but is too vague to identify any specific problem — what string? where? when?
2. Body is the raw bug report template, completely unfilled — zero user-written content
3. A maintainer cannot even formulate a follow-up question — there is no specific behavior, feature, or scenario to ask about
4. This is not an `~info-needed` candidate; it's spam. An info-needed issue has enough context to ask a meaningful question ("can you describe the error in more detail?"). This issue provides no thread to pull on

**Key lesson:** A title that uses real technical words does NOT make the issue legitimate. "Invalid string length issue" sounds plausible, but paired with a completely empty body, it provides nothing actionable. The distinction from `~info-needed`: there must be enough context to formulate a follow-up question.

---

### Example 13: Single Technical Word + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#307397

- **Title:** "Error"
- **Body:** Bug report template with only HTML comments and empty fields. No user-written content.

**Why SPAM:**
1. "Error" as a standalone title tells maintainers nothing — what error? where? what were you doing?
2. Body is completely unfilled — the user submitted the raw template without writing anything
3. There is literally nothing a maintainer could ask about — "Can you tell us about the error?" is the only possible question, and it should have been in the issue to begin with

---

### Example 14: Vague Description Title + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#303897

- **Title:** "Vs Code Error"
- **Body:** Bug report template with only HTML comments and empty fields. No user-written content.

**Why SPAM:**
1. "Vs Code Error" is slightly more specific than "Error" but still far too vague — it just restates the product name and the word "error"
2. Body is entirely auto-generated template text, completely unfilled
3. Same pattern as Example 13 — no context for any meaningful follow-up

---

### Example 15: Longer Vague Title + Empty Template

**Verdict: SPAM** — Source: microsoft/vscode#307813

- **Title:** "I'm not sure what happneend, but such error comes frequently in the past days..."
- **Body:** Bug report template with only HTML comments and empty fields. No user-written content.

**Why SPAM:**
1. Despite being a longer, natural-language title with a typo ("happneend"), the title does not describe any specific behavior — what error? in what context? what frequency?
2. Body is completely unfilled — the user put their entire thought into the title and submitted the empty template
3. A longer title does not compensate for a completely empty body — the issue is still unactionable

**Key lesson:** Title length alone doesn't make an issue legitimate. Even multi-word, grammatically correct titles that sound like a human describing a problem are spam when paired with a completely empty template body. The body must contain user-written content.

---

## CLEAN Examples

### Example 16: Frustrated But Legitimate

**Verdict: CLEAN**

- **Title:** "Autocomplete is completely broken after update"
- **Body:** "Ever since the last update, autocomplete suggestions are wrong. I type `console.` and get completely unrelated suggestions. This is really frustrating — it was working fine before. Steps: 1. Open any .ts file 2. Type `console.` 3. See wrong suggestions"

**Why CLEAN:**
1. No profanity — frustrated tone is fine ("really frustrating", "completely broken")
2. Clear description of the problem
3. Includes reproduction steps
4. Describes expected vs actual behavior

---

### Example 17: Non-English But Legitimate

**Verdict: CLEAN**

- **Title:** "エディターがクラッシュする" (Editor crashes)
- **Body:** Technical description in Japanese with steps to reproduce

**Why CLEAN:**
1. Non-English issues are not spam
2. Contains legitimate technical content
3. Describes a real software problem

---

### Example 18: Specific Title + Empty Template (Boundary Case)

**Verdict: CLEAN**

- **Title:** "Python extension crashes on import in large workspace"
- **Body:** Bug report template with empty fields — no user-written content beyond the title

**Why CLEAN:**
1. The title names a specific component (Python extension), a specific action (import), and a specific condition (large workspace)
2. Even though the body is an empty template, a maintainer CAN formulate follow-up questions: "What version of the Python extension? What file are you importing? How large is the workspace?"
3. This is an `~info-needed` candidate, not spam — there is enough context in the title to identify a specific scenario and ask for more details

**Key lesson:** The line between spam and info-needed for empty-template issues is whether the title provides enough context for a meaningful follow-up. "Error" provides nothing to ask about. "Python extension crashes on import in large workspace" provides a component, action, and condition — that's enough to follow up on.
